5f9R9MtkpqM.summary: Cognitive scientist George Lakoff lectures on how political debates are framed through language and metaphors tied to values, and on the moral worldviews behind progressive and conservative politics. It was given in 2005 at UC San Diego.
5f9R9MtkpqM.why: HN commenters repeatedly say it changed how they hear political speech and recommend it for understanding why opponents are not simply stupid.

5SaFTm2bcac.summary: Nate Harrison's 2004 video history of the Amen Break, a six-second drum sample from a 1969 b-side that became the basis of hip-hop sampling, jungle and drum and bass. It is also a meditation on cultural ownership and creativity.
5SaFTm2bcac.why: A perennial HN recommendation, brought up whenever sampling, copyright or music history comes up, often described as a must-watch.

5ESJH1NLMLs.summary: A re-upload of American Airlines captain Warren Vanderburgh's 1997 presentation warning that pilots who over-rely on cockpit automation lose manual flying skills and awareness. The uploader adds context from his own flying.
5ESJH1NLMLs.why: HN brings it up in any thread about autopilot, Tesla FSD, self-driving cars and crashes as the classic lecture on automation dependency.

5IUj1EZwpJY.summary: Casey Muratori's lecture, originally given at the Technical University of Madrid, arguing that Conway's Law is the only viable candidate for a true law of software architecture. He explains how software mimics the organization over time, using examples like Windows' multiple volume controls.
5IUj1EZwpJY.why: HN treats it as the definitive explanation of Conway's Law and links it in almost any thread about org structure shaping software.

5Ge2RcvDlgw.summary: Asianometry explains the EUV light source inside ASML's lithography machines, where lasers hit falling tin droplets twice to produce 13.5 nm light. It walks through the engineering of the droplet generator, the pre-pulse and main laser, and the plasma that results.
5Ge2RcvDlgw.why: Commenters repeatedly point to it whenever EUV, ASML or chip manufacturing comes up, as a clear and astonishing explanation of one of the hardest engineering problems in chipmaking.

5YV_iKnzDRg.summary: Dr. Roger Seheult of MedCram reviews the benefits of sunlight beyond vitamin D, covering the solar spectrum, circadian rhythm, melatonin and infrared light. The lecture runs nearly two hours with timestamps.
5YV_iKnzDRg.why: HN cites it as an accessible physician-led review supporting claims about infrared light, mitochondria and morning sun.

5PmHRSeA2c8.summary: A 72-minute Q&A with Linus Torvalds at DebConf 14. Topics include the pain of distributing Linux binaries, distro fragmentation, kernel backwards compatibility, GPLv2 versus GPLv3 and conduct.
5PmHRSeA2c8.why: HN returns to it as Linus's own explanation of why shipping software on Linux is hard and why he dislikes GPLv3.

5TFDG-y-EHs.summary: Tom Murphy (suckerpinch) presents a deliberately trollish computer architecture built on IEEE-754 floating point, using NaN and infinity to define logic gates. He builds working hardware around the idea.
5TFDG-y-EHs.why: HN fans hold it up as a favorite among his videos and an example of gloriously bonkers technical art, and cite it in floating-point discussions.

5pYeoZaoWrA.summary: Dan Olson's long Folding Ideas video on the GameStop meme stock phenomenon, its online community and the conspiracy thinking around it. It runs over two hours.
5pYeoZaoWrA.why: Recommended as a thorough, sober critique of meme-stock culture and a good starting point whenever GameStop news appears.

54l8_ewcOlY.summary: The first episode of John Vervaeke's lecture series on the modern meaning crisis, tracing its history through philosophy, cognitive science, religion and psychology. It introduces the series and its themes.
54l8_ewcOlY.why: HN recommends the series as a thorough, non-dogmatic look at meaning, spirituality and escaping nihilism.

5_KcQt0z-eE.summary: A ten-minute card-magic act by Dani DaOrtiz performed on Penn & Teller: Fool Us in 2022. It is built on timing, misdirection and psychology, and the method defeated the show's hosts.
5_KcQt0z-eE.why: HN commenters repeatedly call it among the best magic performances ever, valuing it as acting and craft that stays impressive even once you know the method.

52Mx0_8YEtg.summary: A 2007 Channel 4 documentary by Martin Durkin arguing that human-caused global warming is overstated or a scam. It features contrarian scientists such as Richard Lindzen and promotes sunspot and cosmic-ray explanations for temperature change. Its claims are rejected by mainstream climate science.
52Mx0_8YEtg.why: Climate-skeptic commenters link it as evidence against the CO2 consensus, while others cite it as an example of climate-change denial.

5TkIe60y2GI.summary: Matt Parker talks Numberphile through the different kinds of numbers: algebraic, transcendental, computable, normal, and beyond. It shows how few numbers we can actually name or describe.
5TkIe60y2GI.why: HN recommends it as an accessible explanation of number categories and why almost all numbers are unknowable.

5eW6Eagr9XA.summary: Veritasium examines which experts have real expertise, drawing on chess research and work by Klein and Kahneman. It explains that expertise comes from pattern recognition built through deliberate practice in valid, feedback-rich environments.
5eW6Eagr9XA.why: Frequently recommended in threads on learning, the 10,000 hours rule and deliberate practice as a clearer account of how expertise develops.

5MgBikgcWnY.summary: Josh Kaufman's TEDx talk argues that you can reach practical competence in almost any skill with about 20 hours of focused practice, rather than the 10,000 hours often quoted. He describes how becoming a parent led him to rethink how adults learn, and lays out a short method for rapid skill acquisition.
5MgBikgcWnY.why: HN uses it as the standard counterpoint to the 10,000-hour rule and as an encouraging recipe for starting new skills.

5eo8nz_niiM.summary: Overclocker der8auer tours Hetzner's Falkenstein data center in Germany, showing custom racks, own mainboards, passively cooled servers and ATX-style cases on shelves.
5eo8nz_niiM.why: HN points to it whenever Hetzner comes up, as the best look inside their unusual, semi-custom and low-cost data center setup.

5uljtqyBLxI.summary: Cliff Click of Azul Systems gives a Google Tech Talk on running Java business applications on a machine with about a thousand cores. He covers hardware and software codesign, including garbage collection hardware and the JIT.
5uljtqyBLxI.why: HN treats Cliff Click's talks as an excellent source on JVMs, garbage collection and hardware-assisted Java.

5pdPrQFjo2o.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on the US opioid epidemic, tracing how prescription painkillers fed addiction and heroin use. It is the first of three episodes the show devoted to the crisis.
5pdPrQFjo2o.why: HN points to it as an informative, fact-heavy overview of the opioid crisis and Purdue Pharma.

5wAo54DHDY0.summary: A long video essay on MyHouse.wad, a Doom II mod uploaded by an anonymous user that hides unsettling secrets in its walls. It tells the story of the map, its mystery and its liminal horror.
5wAo54DHDY0.why: Strongly recommended as a gripping story and art piece worth watching even if you do not care about games.

5hVmeOCJjOU.summary: Sean Carroll gives a Royal Institution talk tracing the history of quantum mechanics from Einstein and Bohr to today. He covers the Copenhagen interpretation and the many worlds interpretation.
5hVmeOCJjOU.why: Recommended as an approachable entry point to quantum interpretations, and cited on many worlds questions.

5AqbCQuK0gM.summary: A Channel 9 conversation recorded at GOTO 2012 between Anders Hejlsberg (TypeScript) and Lars Bak (Dart). They discuss the two languages and different approaches to making JavaScript development safer, including runtime type checking.
5AqbCQuK0gM.why: HN points to it as a rare side-by-side of the TypeScript and Dart designers, often to show how the two approaches to improving JavaScript differed.

5WPB2u8EzL8.summary: A Virginia Tech presentation by Sid Smith about collapse, fossil fuels and overshoot, arguing that industrial civilization faces a decline and how one might live with that. It was later expanded into a video series.
5WPB2u8EzL8.why: Recommended in collapse and energy threads as a sobering thermodynamic view of civilization, often with a warning that it is heavy.

5fG_lyNuEAw.summary: Jordan Walke, creator of React, talks at ReasonConf 2019 about the ideas behind ReasonML and how it extends React's programming model with OCaml. He also discusses why familiar syntax matters.
5fG_lyNuEAw.why: HN recommends it as the best introduction to Reason's motivations, straight from React's creator.

5HbYScltf1c.summary: Louis C.K. on Conan explains why he won't give his kids cell phones. He argues that phones keep people from sitting with sadness and being alone with their thoughts, and that kids lose empathy when they cannot see another person's reaction.
5HbYScltf1c.why: Commenters bring it up in threads on phones, boredom, attention and children's screen use as a funny but resonant take.

5Tek9h3a5wQ.summary: The 1965 Cambridge Union debate between James Baldwin and William F. Buckley on race, justice and history in America. Baldwin argues that the American dream came at the expense of Black Americans.
5Tek9h3a5wQ.why: Held up as a classic debate with a clear winner and Baldwin's powerful oratory, still relevant today.

5zkC9IMQmYA.summary: Climber Chris Warner talks at Google about his book on high altitude leadership and the 2007 K2 expedition, where eighteen climbers summited and two died.
5zkC9IMQmYA.why: Strongly recommended as a gripping hour on K2 and on leadership and summit fever in extreme conditions.

52KLGqDSAjo.summary: The first video in potholer54's climate series, giving a basic look at how climate scientists infer that man-made carbon gases are changing the climate. It is a short explainer meant to present the scientific evidence plainly.
52KLGqDSAjo.why: HN users point to it as a clear, evidence-based series to counter climate skepticism.

5Dnw46eC-0o.summary: John Rauser's Strata 2014 keynote argues that programmers can learn statistics quickly by simulating random processes and shuffling data. He explains p-values through resampling rather than formulas.
5Dnw46eC-0o.why: HN recommends it as an excellent programmer-friendly explanation of p-values and statistical thinking.

5Dw3aKbw5Wo.summary: Musician and audio engineer Benn Jordan tries Dolby Atmos as a consumer, covering the theory of immersive audio, its business model, and home theater and headphone listening. He concludes it often falls short of the pitch.
5Dw3aKbw5Wo.why: HN points to it in Atmos and spatial audio threads as a knowledgeable critique of why the format rarely delivers.

5JYp9eGC3Cc.summary: A short clip of the McMurtry Speirling fan car setting a new Goodwood Hill record of 39.08 seconds at the 2022 Festival of Speed, driven by Max Chilton. It beat the previous timed shootout record set in 1999 and the outright record held by the VW ID.R.
5JYp9eGC3Cc.why: HN points to it as a striking demonstration of fan-downforce EVs, with a run that looks glued to the track and almost sped up.

5MdSE-N0bxs.summary: Max Tegmark's MIT CBMM talk on why deep learning works so well. He argues that the laws of physics and the symmetries in physical data make it compressible into small neural networks, tying physics to network structure.
5MdSE-N0bxs.why: HN recommends it as a clear argument for why deep and cheap learning succeeds, often alongside the associated paper.

5MxH1sfJLBQ.summary: Breaking Taps explains how the cryogenic mirror actuators on the James Webb Space Telescope achieve nanometer precision using flexures. It shows a 3D-printed replica and how one motor handles both coarse and fine motion.
5MxH1sfJLBQ.why: Commenters repeatedly recommend it in JWST threads as a great explanation of clever mechanical design that is accurate and long lasting.

5QwOpRh-IfI.summary: A short Tracklib video visualizing the disco sample that Daft Punk's One More Time is built from. It shows how the track is composed from the original material.
5QwOpRh-IfI.why: HN recommends it as a striking visual breakdown of how the song was constructed.

5RKbSi87J5Q.summary: Nardwuar interviews Pharrell and Shay of N.E.R.D. in Vancouver, using his trademark deep research and gifts. The extended version runs about ten minutes.
5RKbSi87J5Q.why: HN holds it up as a model of interview preparation, where thorough research on the guest impresses the interviewee.

5Vt8zqhHe_c.summary: Maciej Ceglowski's talk at Web Directions argues that small teams and lone programmers can build sustainable businesses without chasing Silicon Valley's grow-or-die model. He offers alternative, more achievable definitions of success.
5Vt8zqhHe_c.why: HN regards it as an inspiring, funny case for modest, bootstrapped success over venture-funded risk.

5gnpCqsXE8g.summary: A 1983 Los Angeles lecture by KGB defector Yuri Bezmenov on how the Soviets carried out ideological subversion of target societies through propaganda. He walks through demoralization and normalization stages.
5gnpCqsXE8g.why: HN commenters link it to argue that cultural subversion and normalization are playing out today, though mostly as a reference in unrelated threads.

5guXaWwQpe4.summary: Energy scholar Vaclav Smil argues that global energy transitions are slow and that renewable targets should not rest on wishful thinking. He appraises how energy dependencies are likely to change and asks for using much less.
5guXaWwQpe4.why: HN recommends it as a grounded, data-driven counter to hype about quick energy revolutions.

5tSTk1083VY.summary: Joe Rogan interviews David Goggins, a retired Navy SEAL and ultramarathon runner, about his path from overweight to elite endurance athlete and pushing beyond comfort zones.
5tSTk1083VY.why: HN commenters recommend it as an inspiring story about perseverance and getting outside one's comfort zone.

5u7euN1HTuU.summary: A 98-minute LEMMiNO video reconstructing what happened inside the Texas School Book Depository before, during, and after the Kennedy assassination. It draws on testimony to map people's movements and discrepancies.
5u7euN1HTuU.why: HN recommends it as a detailed, well-sourced overview that helps viewers form their own opinion.

5AVO1IyfA9M.summary: A hobbyist compares vertical bifacial solar panels against south-facing angled panels using winter production results. It tests whether the usual mounting approach is actually best.
5AVO1IyfA9M.why: HN points to it as real-world, side-by-side data on vertical versus angled panel orientation.

5Q9x16uIsKA.summary: Dan Friedman and William Byrd demonstrate miniKanren, a logic programming system for Scheme, in an unconference talk. It includes generating programs by running relations in reverse.
5Q9x16uIsKA.why: HN recommends it as a mind-blowing and fun introduction to logic programming for working programmers.

5SJm2ep3X_M.summary: Peter Rizun and Andrew Stone present results of tests running 1 GB blocks on a Bitcoin test network at Scaling Bitcoin Stanford. The talk argues for big-block scaling and discusses its consequences.
5SJm2ep3X_M.why: Cited by big-block advocates as evidence that Bitcoin could handle far higher throughput.

5cWck_xcH64.summary: Dan Tentler's DEF CON 20 talk on odd things he found on the internet through Shodan, such as stoplights, power systems and other non-computer devices exposed online. It highlights how many devices need no credentials.
5cWck_xcH64.why: HN points to it when discussing exposed IoT and industrial devices, as an eye-opening look at how much is reachable online.

5jdEG_ACXLw.summary: An NFB documentary about the shipbreaking yards of Alang, India, where about 40,000 people dismantle huge ships by hand in dangerous conditions.
5jdEG_ACXLw.why: HN recommends it for an up-close look at the shipbreaking industry.

5kj5ApnhPAE.summary: A 13-minute OSCON 2010 talk in which Rob Pike argues about what is wrong with mainstream languages like C++, Java and C#, and presents Go as a response. He discusses verbosity and what lightness means in a language.
5kj5ApnhPAE.why: HN uses it as a concise statement of the thinking behind Go's design.

5KiC03_wVjc.summary: In Top Gear's second part, racing driver Sabine Schmitz tries to lap the Nurburgring in a Ford Transit van in under ten minutes. She finishes just over the mark.
5KiC03_wVjc.why: Shared in threads about the Nurburgring and after Schmitz's death as a charming showcase of her skill.

5RpPTRcz1no.summary: A political commentary video arguing that tech billionaires such as Thiel, Musk and Andreessen, along with figures like Yarvin, are using the new administration to push their agenda. It connects Yarvin's ideas with Project 2025.
5RpPTRcz1no.why: HN commenters share it during DOGE and government-cuts threads as a summary of the billionaires' aims, though many only cite it as a reference.

5XDTQLa3NjE.summary: Karen Sandler's keynote at Linux.conf.au 2012 on the software running inside medical devices such as her own pacemaker-defibrillator. She discusses the difficulty of learning what code runs in life-sustaining devices and why open source matters there.
5XDTQLa3NjE.why: HN commenters point to it in threads about medical device security and software transparency as an excellent, personal case for open source in implants.

5hUT8VZNvm8.summary: Journalist Vincent Woo discusses his New York Magazine piece on Lambda School's misleading promises, including its income share agreements and placement claims, in an interview on This Week in Startups. The host questions him pointedly.
5hUT8VZNvm8.why: HN cites it in Lambda School threads as a revealing interview that lends credibility to Woo's reporting.

5sVfTPaxRwk.summary: A Kurzgesagt video on the conditions in which most farm animals are raised. It argues that cruelty is for cheaper rather than better meat, and that a small price increase per meal could avoid most of the suffering.
5sVfTPaxRwk.why: Recommended as a clear, evidence-backed introduction to the economics of animal welfare in meat and egg production.

5uhIiI9Ld5M.summary: Andy Bell's 2022 talk on hinting the browser rather than micromanaging it, using progressive enhancement, CSS layout, fluid type and space, and modern CSS to build resilient front-ends.
5uhIiI9Ld5M.why: HN recommends it as a practical case for intrinsic, fluid CSS that cuts down on media queries and selectors.

586Zn1ct-QA.summary: EEVblog interviews Richard Stephenson of NASA's Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex about how the 70m DSS-43 dish is used to contact Voyager 2. It covers the ground antenna and low-noise receiver side of deep space communication. This is a 2023 re-release of a 2017 video.
586Zn1ct-QA.why: Shared in Voyager news threads as an accessible look at the real equipment used to talk to the probes.

5BIP_N9qQm4.summary: The SILE author's FOSDEM 2015 talk introducing SILE, a TeX-inspired typesetting system with frame-based layout, Unicode, OpenType and a Lua-based extensible design.
5BIP_N9qQm4.why: Pointed to as the standard introduction to SILE as a modern TeX alternative, though possibly dated.

5ODzO7Lz_pw.summary: Designer Thomas Thwaites describes his attempt to build a toaster from scratch, from mining ore and deriving plastic from oil. It is a short TED talk on how much civilization a simple object depends on.
5ODzO7Lz_pw.why: HN uses it as the standard illustration of hidden complexity and supply-chain dependencies behind everyday objects.

5P5Mk_IggE0.summary: A two-hour Oxide and Friends session answering questions after shipping the first Oxide rack. Topics include making hardware as a startup and why Oxide chose illumos.
5P5Mk_IggE0.why: HN cites it as Oxide's own explanation of how they ship hardware as a startup and why they picked illumos.

5V1ynVyud4M.summary: Chris Granger presents Eve, a programming environment designed to be approachable for humans, at Strange Loop 2015. The talk covers the project's approach and design ideas.
5V1ynVyud4M.why: HN mentions it as one of the talks on Eve, usually as related prior work in discussions of end-user and visual programming.

5ZjhNTM8XU8.summary: Martin Kleppmann's Strange Loop talk on database transactions, covering why they were dropped by NoSQL, their reputation for being slow, and newer algorithms that make serializable transactions perform and scale. It touches on consistency, linearizability and the CAP theorem.
5ZjhNTM8XU8.why: Recommended as a compact preview of Kleppmann's data systems material, including from his book on the subject.

5_-Ac68FKG4.summary: Asianometry traces how the Japanese zaibatsu families grew into vast industrial combines and how postwar reforms abruptly broke up their wealth and control.
5_-Ac68FKG4.why: Recommended as a look at how Japan's monopolies were dismantled and how that shaped later industry.

5d6SEQQbwtU.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day documents boarding a US Navy nuclear submarine in the Arctic during the ICEX 2020 under-ice exercise. It is the first of a series on life aboard a fast attack submarine.
5d6SEQQbwtU.why: Recommended in submarine threads as the start of an access-rich series on life aboard a US fast attack sub.

5eBT6OSr1TI.summary: A comedy song by Dan and Dan that summarizes the British newspaper The Daily Mail using only its headlines. It satirizes the paper's habit of claiming everything causes or cures cancer.
5eBT6OSr1TI.why: Used as a running joke or satirical shorthand whenever the Daily Mail is cited or criticized.

5eqRuVp65eY.summary: A Welch Labs explainer on neural scaling laws and the compute-efficient frontier, asking why model loss seems to hit a line it cannot cross. It draws an analogy to an ideal gas law for AI.
5eqRuVp65eY.why: Recommended as a well-made, digestible introduction to scaling laws and why models cluster along a similar efficiency frontier.

5fbvquHSPJU.summary: An independent feature documentary in which 23 economists, advisers and financiers discuss how the financial system works and what a more just economic model might look like. It covers money creation, debt and the aftermath of the financial crisis.
5fbvquHSPJU.why: Mentioned as a one-package overview of heterodox views on money creation and debt, though some find it unsurprising.

5pidokakU4I.summary: Australian comedy group Axis of Awesome perform a sketch showing that dozens of pop hits share the same four chords. It was recorded at the 2009 Melbourne International Comedy Festival.
5pidokakU4I.why: The go-to reference in threads on chord progressions, pop music similarity and music copyright.

5q-BH-tvxEg.summary: Arthur Ganson's kinetic sculpture chains twelve 1:50 worm gear reductions so the final gear, embedded in concrete, would take over two trillion years to turn once.
5q-BH-tvxEg.why: Shared whenever gear reductions, exponential scaling or playful kinetic art come up.

5tu32CCA_Ig.summary: A short RepresentUs explainer arguing that US politics is shaped by money, citing the Gilens and Page Princeton study on how little average citizens influence policy.
5tu32CCA_Ig.why: Frequently linked as a compact summary of the Princeton study when commenters argue Congress ignores public opinion.

5uiroWBkdFY.summary: A three-minute demonstration of professional hand-soldering techniques for multi-lead surface mount parts, to IPC class 3 criteria.
5uiroWBkdFY.why: HN points to it as proof that SMD soldering is simpler than people fear.

5FWWe2U41N8.summary: Insider Food visits the Gurudwara Bangla Sahib temple in New Delhi, which feeds tens of thousands of people free daily and over 100,000 on holidays. It shows the machines and big-batch cooking that make this possible.
5FWWe2U41N8.why: HN cites it as an example of efficient, machine-assisted mass feeding of people for free.

5BXtgq0Nhsc.summary: A short clip, from 2003, of Noam Chomsky going through crimes of post-WW2 US presidents. He argues that they would be indictable under the Nuremberg principles.
5BXtgq0Nhsc.why: HN links it as the source for the claim that every post-war president would be indictable under Nuremberg standards.

5CzURm7OpAA.summary: A DEF CON 23 talk on researching whether a commercial quadcopter could be forced to land by interfering with its GPS signal, inspired by a neighbor's kid's drone. It covers the research and the legal and technical issues encountered.
5CzURm7OpAA.why: HN brings it up in drone threads as a favorite tech talk and as evidence of how weak consumer drone security is.

5It1zarINv0.summary: A long interview with former KGB agent Yuri Bezmenov describing what he calls ideological subversion, a process of demoralizing a nation. He claims it works by influencing academia and media over years.
5It1zarINv0.why: HN commenters mostly cite it in political threads as a theory of subversion, and several mentions are repeated drive-by posts.

5OtKEetGy2Y.summary: A video essay by Tom Nicholas critiquing Elon Musk's futurism, covering SpaceX's Mars plans, Tesla versus Ford and the idea of a slow cancellation of the future. It asks whom Musk's vision of the future serves.
5OtKEetGy2Y.why: Cited in Musk-related threads as a critical perspective on his futurism and his projects, such as hyperloop.

5S7Bb0Qg-oE.summary: Max Miller of Tasting History makes garum, the fermented fish sauce of ancient Rome, using a same-day recipe. He covers the history of the condiment along the way.
5S7Bb0Qg-oE.why: HN cites it in threads on Roman food and fish sauce as a hands-on demonstration of making garum.

5SBo0akeDMY.summary: A 2014 BBC Newsnight report by Gabriel Gatehouse on the presence and influence of far-right and neo-Nazi groups in the new Ukrainian government after the Maidan. It is a short news investigation.
5SBo0akeDMY.why: Cited in Ukraine and Russia threads as older mainstream coverage of far-right groups in Ukraine, mostly as a reference in political arguments rather than recommended viewing.

5_A8dq2fA5o.summary: A New Yorker short documentary about the 2014 sinking of the Sewol ferry in South Korea, based on the film In the Absence. It examines the failures in the rescue and the political aftermath.
5_A8dq2fA5o.why: HN mostly cites it as an example of institutional failure and deference to hierarchy during a disaster.

5bQhGS8V6dQ.summary: Christian Schafmeister presents CANDO at the 2016 European Lisp Symposium. It is a compiled Lisp-based language for designing macromolecules and nanoscale materials, built on the Clasp implementation of Common Lisp.
5bQhGS8V6dQ.why: Recommended as one of the best talks of the symposium for the unusual scope of applying Lisp to molecular design.

5eL_LcxwwHg.summary: Andrew Kelley's 2024 Zig roadmap talk, followed by a Q&A, covers the language's priorities and the state of the project. Topics include compilation speed, moving off LLVM toward a self-hosted toolchain, async, and the path to 1.0.
5eL_LcxwwHg.why: HN points to it as the authoritative source on Zig's direction, especially why async was removed and why the toolchain is changing.

5nW3nJhBHL0.summary: Stand-up Maths explains why the perimeter of an ellipse has no simple closed-form equation, showing the infinite series and presenting approximation formulas.
5nW3nJhBHL0.why: Cited as an accessible explanation of why some simple shapes lack neat exact formulas.

5t1vTLU7s40.summary: Lex Fridman's long podcast interview with Yann LeCun on Meta AI, open source, the limits of LLMs, AGI and the future of AI.
5t1vTLU7s40.why: Cited for LeCun's views on LLM limits and alternative approaches to intelligence.

5t5QK03KXPc.summary: President Reagan's 1987 radio address on free and fair trade, in which he argues for free trade over protectionism.
5t5QK03KXPc.why: Cited in tariff debates to show Reagan's own words against protectionism.

5v1Yg6XejyE.summary: Channel 4 News reports on undercover Greenpeace footage of an ExxonMobil lobbyist describing efforts to weaken climate legislation. Exxon disputes the claims.
5v1Yg6XejyE.why: Cited as a source on oil industry lobbying and disinformation in climate policy threads.

5zW9_ztTiw8.summary: Tech Ingredients shows how to build a liquid panel with a specialty paint that, placed outside, cools below ambient air temperature. It demonstrates radiative sky cooling.
5zW9_ztTiw8.why: HN points to it in threads on radiative cooling as a hands-on explanation of passive daytime cooling.

5-OjTPj7K54.summary: Julia Ecklar's recording of "The Eternal Flame," a filk song about God writing the universe in Lisp, written by Bob Kanefsky. It is a geek-humor song set to a familiar tune.
5-OjTPj7K54.why: HN mostly references it as Lisp-culture humor and a nod to Kanefsky's song.

590cy1biewc.summary: A short NYT Op-Doc by Laura Poitras profiling NSA veteran William Binney, who says a program he helped design collects Americans' personal data.
590cy1biewc.why: HN cites Binney's testimony in debates about NSA domestic surveillance.

5AwdkGKmZ0I.summary: Apple's November 10, 2020 event introducing the Apple M1 chip and the new MacBook Air, 13-inch MacBook Pro and Mac mini, along with macOS Big Sur.
5AwdkGKmZ0I.why: Cited as the primary source for Apple's M1 performance claims, such as fastest CPU core and performance per watt.

5GMXqgQIU9c.summary: Josef Holzer walks through his family's Krameterhof, one of Europe's oldest permaculture farms in the Austrian mountains, with fish ponds, terraces, fruit trees and grazing animals. It showcases water management and microclimates.
5GMXqgQIU9c.why: HN cites it as a realistic example of productive mountain farming and of growing hardy crops in cold alpine conditions.

5GpOfwbFRcs.summary: A short 2010 parody sketch titled 'All The Cool Kids Use Ruby' about an absurd initial consultation. It is a spoof of tech-hype culture.
5GpOfwbFRcs.why: Used as a joke reference whenever the cool-kids-use-X trope comes up in technology threads.

5HDN9fUlqU8.summary: A short BicycleDutch episode showing how Dutch junctions with protected cycle paths are laid out. It argues these are proven, non-experimental designs that make intersections safer for cyclists.
5HDN9fUlqU8.why: Linked as the go-to demonstration that the cyclist-versus-driver conflict at intersections is a solved design problem.

5J3H8--CQRE.summary: Engineering Explained follows up on Tesla's claim that a Cybertruck towing a Porsche 911 could beat the 911 alone over a quarter mile. He walks through the MotorTrend drag race and explains why the claim did not hold up.
5J3H8--CQRE.why: HN uses it almost entirely as evidence in criticism of Tesla's marketing claims, repeating that Tesla never ran the quarter mile it advertised.

5KKDCp3OaMo.summary: Tom Gally, a former professional translator and University of Tokyo professor, discusses in March 2023 whether GPT-4 and similar models could translate literary and popular fiction. He gives his assessment of Japanese-to-English quality.
5KKDCp3OaMo.why: Cited as an expert's first-hand evidence that GPT translation is near human quality for distant language pairs.

5McECUtM8fw.summary: Cockpit footage of an approach to the Megeve altiport in France that ends in a gear-up landing, with the warning horn audible throughout. Everyone aboard survived and the crew had thousands of flight hours.
5McECUtM8fw.why: Cited as a vivid example that experienced pilots can ignore loud alarms, in threads on alarm design and gear-up landings.

5PmphkNDosg.summary: A commentary video by YouTuber PaymoneyWubby reacting to children's content on the Musical.ly app, which became TikTok. It highlights the child-safety concerns of young kids dancing on a public social platform.
5PmphkNDosg.why: Cited as an outsider's critical look at Musical.ly and TikTok and the child-safety problems of video platforms.

5QQdNbvSGok.summary: The short printer-destruction-adjacent clip from Office Space built around the cryptic 'PC LOAD LETTER' error message. It pokes fun at unhelpful printer errors.
5QQdNbvSGok.why: Used as a joke reference in threads about confusing error messages and printers.

5YGc4zOqozo.summary: Dave Carroll's song and music video about United Airlines baggage handlers breaking his Taylor guitar and the airline's refusal to compensate him. It became a viral example of a customer fighting a company.
5YGc4zOqozo.why: Used as the classic example of terrible airline customer service, and of how a viral video can force a company to respond.

5c6AADI7Pb4.summary: Bryan Seely tells how he used fake Google Maps business listings to intercept phone calls meant for the Secret Service and FBI. He then turned himself in, and the talk explains the verification gaps that made it possible.
5c6AADI7Pb4.why: Referenced as a concrete example of how weak Google Maps listing verification enables phone fraud and impersonation.

5gT5NULvRSk.summary: A 2018 local news report showing people using drugs openly in the corridors of San Francisco's Civic Center BART station.
5gT5NULvRSk.why: Used by commenters as illustrative evidence in critical discussions about San Francisco's drug and homelessness problems.

5iV_hB08Uns.summary: A short Boston Dynamics demo of Handle, a wheeled mobile manipulation robot that builds and unloads mixed-box pallets in a warehouse. It uses vision to find boxes and force control to place them against neighbors.
5iV_hB08Uns.why: Mostly cited as an example of robots doing warehouse and logistics work in automation discussions.

5nKk_-Lvhzo.summary: SANS ICS Security's parody video of the HyperEncabulator, a spoof of the Turbo Encabulator technobabble videos.
5nKk_-Lvhzo.why: Only brought up as a joke about encabulator-style nonsense jargon.

5pNL7MlUpmI.summary: A Some More News episode critical of Elon Musk, covering his public image, billionaire behavior, the Boring Company and the push to Mars.
5pNL7MlUpmI.why: Mostly cited as an example of criticism of Musk, not recommended as a neutral source.

5rXPrfnU3G0.summary: WikiLeaks' release of cockpit footage from a 2007 US Apache helicopter attack in Baghdad that killed a group of men including two Reuters staff, and then a van that came to help the wounded. The video includes the crew's radio chatter and context on the military's initial account.
5rXPrfnU3G0.why: HN cites it as the key evidence of what Chelsea Manning leaked and as an example of civilian deaths in war, with some early commenters disputing how to read the footage.

5s5EvhHy7eQ.summary: Johnny Chung Lee shows how infrared light pens and a Wii Remote can make a very low-cost multi-point interactive whiteboard or tablet display. Software is available for download.
5s5EvhHy7eQ.why: HN cites it as a clever low-budget hardware hack and as an example of novel Wiimote uses that never became commercial.

5sVOSlUn7e0.summary: A short clip of a ramen restaurant in Nagoya where robot arms cook the noodles. Human waiters serve the food.
5sVOSlUn7e0.why: Used as an early, concrete example of robotic kitchen automation when HN discusses robot chefs and baristas.

5uxsFglz2ig.summary: A short video of railroad workers in Storfors, Sweden, using thermite to weld rail sections together.
5uxsFglz2ig.why: Cited as a concrete example of how thermite is used for track welding in discussions of rail and thermite.
